name: nt-send-test
focus: /** What to say for a state change
prompt: In web/src/core/desknotify.ts add a new exported function `sendTest` directly above the comment `/** What to say for a state change, or null when it is not worth a notification. */`. Signature: `export async function sendTest(): Promise<{ ok: boolean; detail: string }>`. It sends one notification with title "Kompanion test" and body "If you can read this, notifications work.", and it ignores the enabled() switch and the document focus. Tauri path (`(window as any).__TAURI__?.notification` exists): `await isPermissionGranted()`; when false `await requestPermission()` and check again; when still not granted return `{ ok: false, detail: "Notifications are blocked: allow Kompanion in System Settings > Notifications." }`; then `await sendNotification({ title, body })` and return `{ ok: true, detail: "Test notification sent through the desktop app." }`. Wrap the Tauri calls in try/catch: on an error call `console.error("Kompanion test notification failed", e)` and return `{ ok: false, detail: "Test notification failed: " + message }` where message is `e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e)`. Browser path: when `!("Notification" in window)` return `{ ok: false, detail: "This browser cannot show notifications." }`; when `Notification.permission` is not "granted" call `await Notification.requestPermission()` and when the result is not "granted" return `{ ok: false, detail: "Notifications are blocked: allow them for this site in the browser's settings." }`; then `new Notification(title, { body, icon: "/api/mail-logo.png" })` in a try/catch like above and return `{ ok: true, detail: "Test notification sent." }`. Change nothing else.
